svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.15.3.3 Application of Footing Width and Area Requirements
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.15 FOOTINGS AND FOUNDATIONS
Application of Footing Width and Area Requirements

g.text: Supported joist span not more than
Specified live load on any floor not more
Footings under masonry, concrete or ICF
or masonry or ICF walls, floors and roofs

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Except as in Sentence 9.15.3.4.(2), the width
and area requirements of Articles 9.15.3.4. to
9.15.3.7. apply to footings that support
(i) foundation walls of masonry, concrete or flat
ICF, (ii) above-ground walls of masonry, flat ICF
or light wood-frame construction, and (iii)
floors and roofs of light wood-frame
construction, where the span of supported joists
does not exceed 4.9 m (16′-0⅞″) and the specified
live load on any supported floor does not exceed
2.4 kPa (50.1 psf) (see Table 4.1.5.3.).
Except as in Sentence 9.15.3.4.(2), where the
supported joist span exceeds 4.9 m, footings
are designed in accordance with Section 4.2.
Where the specified live load exceeds 2.4 kPa,
footings are designed in accordance with
Section 4.2.
Drawn: a 2-storey house cut through, centre beam on a post. Sizes other than the limits are illustration only.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.15.3.3. (page 9-119)
